Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority states that tariffs and insurance will not be collected from ship owners during the 60-day period of the Islamabad Memorandum.
Norwegian prime minister Jonas Gahr Støre announces new school guidelines that generally prohibit the use of generative AI by primary school pupils and restrict its use for older students.
At least 47 people are killed and 97 more injured by Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon.
The United States announces that Israel and Hezbollah agreed to a ceasefire.
The UN secretary general envoy to Sudan calls for RSF head Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo to halt attacks on the North Kordofan area of El-Obeid.

Philippine president Bongbong Marcos announces that 24 Filipino nationals detained in Russia will be released and repatriated to the Philippines following a meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin in Kazan.
At least ten people are killed and several injured in the past 24 hours, due to strong winds and heavy rain in parts of Pakistan.

Polish president Karol Nawrocki strips Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy of the country's highest honour, the Order of the White Eagle, for naming an army unit after the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which massacred Poles during World War II.
Costa Rican police arrest a man in connection with an alleged threat against president Laura Fernández Delgado.
The president is evacuated during a visit to northern Costa Rica after an explosion was reported nearby.

British home secretary Shabana Mahmood, energy secretary Ed Miliband, and transport secretary Heidi Alexander meet with prime minister Keir Starmer and reportedly urge him to set out a timetable for his departure following Andy Burnham's win in the 2026 Makerfield by-election.
Four Israeli soldiers are killed in a shootout with Hezbollah fighters near Nabatieh, Lebanon.

Lebanese conservationist and environmentalist Mona Khalil, a advocate for the protection of endangered sea turtles, dies from wounds sustained during an Israeli attack in southern Lebanon two weeks ago.

The Sudanese human rights organization Emergency Lawyers reports that nine civilians have been killed in a Rapid Support Forces (RSF) drone strike on a passenger vehicle carrying civilians in North Darfur.
Additionally, another drone struck the Um Bayada market, causing a massive fire.

Indian shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says that three Indian oil tankers, the Desh Vaibhav, Desh Vibhor, and Sanmar Herald, have safely transited through the Strait of Hormuz and are on their way to India.

A Spanish court orders Begoña Gómez, the wife of prime minister Pedro Sánchez, to stand trial on corruption-related charges, confiscates her passport, and restricts her international travel pending proceedings.
The office of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu states that Israeli troops will remain in southern Lebanon to protect Israel's northern border for as long as it is believed to be necessary.

The United States Central Command says that 55 ships transporting more than 17 million barrels of oil and cargo have crossed the strait and that traffic on the chokepoint increased, rejecting Iran’s claims that the waterway is closed.
The Australian Government confirms the first detection of the avian influenza subtype H5N1 in the country after identifying the virus in a wild seabird in Western Australia.
In a major recovery from climate-related disaster, thousands of flamingo eggs hatched at Lake Tuz in Turkey.

The Israeli military and Shin Bet confirm that they have killed Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander Zaki Youssef Mahmoud Abu Mustafa, who participated in the kidnapping of 12-year-old Yagil Yaakov during the Nir Oz attack on October 7, 2023.
Additionally, he was also accused of training jihadists at the Nasser Hospital.
Six people are killed and 29 people are injured as a bus crashes into a parked truck in Jalpaiguri, West Bengal, India.

The last American passenger exits the National Quarantine Unit at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, officially ending the quarantine for Americans who were affected by the hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship.
The Tasnim News Agency reports that Iran will keep the Strait of Hormuz closed until the ceasefire is implemented in the Lebanon war and waivers are issued for Iranian oil sales.
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa says that his country will not intervene in the Israel–Hezbollah conflict in Lebanon following calls from U.S. president Donald Trump to do so.
The first talks between Iran and the United States since the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum are held at the Bürgenstock Resort in Switzerland.
Israeli defense minister Israel Katz says that Israeli troops will not withdraw from the illegally occupied Beaufort Castle, Lebanon.
The Indian government confirms that four India-bound fertilizer cargo ships carrying urea, diammonium phosphate, and sulfur have successfully transited through the Strait of Hormuz.
The United Nations reports that the Tatmadaw's army has killed over 700 Myanmar civilians in six months.
A South Korean court sentences former justice minister Park Sung-jae to 25 years in prison for being involved in former president Yoon Suk Yeol's martial law declaration.
The U.S. treasury department lifts sanctions against Iran and authorizes the production, delivery and sale of Iranian oil for 60 days amidst ongoing talks in Switzerland.
Secretary of State Rubio says that ceasefire talks are ongoing, contradicting Iranian media statements.
A Spanish court sentences former transport minister José Luis Ábalos to 24 years in prison for taking bribes in connection with public contracts for face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic.
His advisor Koldo García is sentenced to 19 years and businessman Víctor de Aldama to four and a half years.
A British court finds former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson guilty of all 18 charges, including one count of rape, in relation to two victims who were children at the time of the offense.
In a related trial of the facts, the jury found that his wife, Eleanor, had aided and abetted five offenses.
Authorities in South Sudan announce that the first general election in the country will be held on December 22, 2026, the first since its independence in 2011.
The United States Senate votes 85–5 to pass the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a bill aimed at lowering the cost-of-living of houses and supporting affordable housing in the country.

Ukrainian deputy prime minister Oleksiy Kuleba says that Russian drone attacks in Ukraine have killed at least five people, including an Egyptian crew member aboard a Panamanian-flagged vessel in the Black Sea and three members of the same family in Sumy Oblast.
The attack also damages the vessel and forces its crew to evacuate.
Mediators Pakistan and Qatar say that Iran and the United States have agreed to a roadmap aimed at reaching a final deal within 60 days.

U.S. crude oil prices fall 2.7% to about $74 per barrel for the first time since early March after treasury secretary Scott Bessent announced a 60-day waiver of sanctions on the purchase of Iranian oil.
At least 15 people are killed, including children, and several others are injured in a fire at a commercial building in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India.
The U.S., Bahraini, and Kuwaiti militaries intercept ballistic missiles and drones fired by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps at U.S. military bases in Bahrain and Kuwait after a U.S.

Employees of the Czech public broadcasters Czech Television and Czech Radio are on a 24-hour warning strike to protest against the abolition of licence fees and tying of the public media budget to the government budget.
At least 15 people are killed and 10 injured after a truck plunged into a ditch between Dhaka and Tangail, Bangladesh.
The total amount of cases of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reaches past 1,000.

The Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, a United Nations fact-finding mission, finds that Israel has deliberately targeted Palestinian children, resulting in genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes in Gaza, and war crimes in the West Bank.
House of Representatives passes the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act in an effort to lower the cost-of-living of houses and support affordable housing in the country.

The International Maritime Organization announces an evacuation plan for around 500 to 600 ships with 11,000 seafarers stranded in the Persian Gulf to sail through the Strait of Hormuz after Iran and the United States have reached a ceasefire deal to end the war.

The Bangladesh Shipping Corporation reports that the Bangladesh-flagged DWT bulk carrier vessel MV Banglar Joyjatra has cleared through the Strait of Hormuz at 3:00am BST after it was stranded in the region for 4.5 months.
France records its hottest ever day on record after a temperature of 44.3°C is recorded in Pissos, Nouvelle-Aquitaine, according to Météo-France.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a Congress testimony says that Iran has agreed to negotiate aspects of its nuclear program despite pausing peace talks and closing the Strait of Hormuz.
Senate votes 50–48 in favor of a resolution to require the Trump administration to halt military action against Iran, joining the House of Representatives in doing so.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio says that the U.S. will not accept Iranian tolls or fees on vessels transiting through the Strait of Hormuz.
Department of Homeland Security eases travel restrictions for the Iranian soccer team, allowing them to arrive in Seattle, Washington two days before their match at Lumen Field against Egypt.
The Israeli military announces that it has killed Hamas militant Akram Muhammad Mahmoud Abu Machi, who took part in the October 7 attacks on Israel, during an airstrike in southern Gaza.
The U.S. military says that it will require recruits to take the influenza vaccine amidst an influenza outbreak at the Lackland Air Force Base in Bexar County, Texas, U.S.
The move comes after U.S. defense secretary Pete Hegseth lifted the military vaccine mandate.

The Sudan Doctors Network reports that more than 215 civilians have died at the RSF-run Daqris Prison in Sudan's South Darfur state from the spread of diseases and epidemics, as well as torture and mistreatment of detainees.
Five people are killed and 20 injured after an under-construction warehouse collapses in West Bengal, India.

Israeli defence minister Israel Katz says his forces will not withdraw from occupied southern Lebanon even if "the United States demands it", adding that "200,000 residents will not return" to their homes.

After the deadly fire in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, that killed 15 people, state authorities close down 59 coaching institutes found to be violating fire safety standards as part of a statewide enforcement drive.
Abelardo de la Espriella is declared president-elect of Colombia by the National Electoral Council.
Ukrainian missiles strike two Russian military airfields and several air defence systems in Crimea.

A South Korean court orders the arrest of Shincheonji Church of Jesus leader Lee Man-hee for allegedly coercing thousands of followers to join the People Power Party in violation of the Political Parties Act.
A monitoring system in Spain estimates that a heat wave contributed to 212 deaths between Sunday and Wednesday.
The country also records its highest average June temperatures since at least 1950.
The Iran-backed militia groups Asaib Ahl al-Haq and Imam Ali Brigades say that they will hand their weapons to the Iraqi government.

In Spain, the Congress of Deputies approves a motion calling on the prime minister Pedro Sánchez to face a vote of confidence following the escalation of corruption cases involving his PSOE party and his family.

Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez says that the International Maritime Organization will pause an evacuation effort for 11,000 seafarers on stranded ships in the Strait of Hormuz after Iran objected to the plan and after a vessel was attacked near Oman.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy rejects United Nations-backed temporary shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz proposed with Oman while negotiations continue over the waterway's future administration.
French president Emmanuel Macron announces that the navy intercepted and boarded the Cameroon-flagged, Russia-linked oil tanker Deliver off the coast of Sicily, Italy, two days earlier.
Israeli defense minister Israel Katz says that the military will keep troops in occupied Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza in Palestine forever.
Department of Commerce reported a 4.1% increase in consumer prices driven by high gas prices, the largest since April 2023.
The International Organization for Migration reports that 1,430 people were displaced from five villages in Sudan's North Darfur state in a single day due to worsening insecurity.
The confirmed toll of yesterday's earthquakes in Venezuela rises to 188 people killed, over 1000 people injured, and more than 36,000 others believed to be missing.

Turkish police seize more than 10,000 historical artifacts during a raid on a residence in Istanbul and arrest two people in connection with an investigation into the alleged illegal possession of cultural property.
Israeli airstrikes are reported in Nabatieh, in other towns of the Nabatieh District, and in the Tyre District, Lebanon, in violation of an ongoing ceasefire.
Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu states that Israeli forces will remain in southern Lebanon until Hezbollah disarms, despite the framework agreement.

The United States Central Command says its forces have conducted airstrikes on Iran in response to yesterday's drone strike on a civilian Singapore-flagged cargo ship transiting the Strait of Hormuz, striking Iranian missile and drone storage sites, and coastal radar sites.

A direct communications line between Iran and the U.S. is established under Article 5 of the memorandum of understanding over the Strait of Hormuz in an effort to prevent incidents that could lead to military confrontation.
Three people die inside of a septic tank during an attempt to clean it in Mundka, Delhi, India.

Netanyahu states that displaced Lebanese civilians will not be permitted to return to areas within the Israeli-controlled security zone in southern Lebanon under arrangements announced following the agreement.
Russia and Ukraine exchange prisoners of war, with each side releasing 160 people.
Seven more bodies are retrieved from the collapsed under-construction building in Angeles, Philippines, raising the death toll to 21.
The confirmed toll of the June 24 earthquakes in Venezuela rises to 920 people killed and over 3,360 injured, with 51,000 reported missing.
The United Nations estimates that the earthquakes caused approximately US$6.7 billion in direct physical damage, equivalent to about 6% of Venezuela's gross domestic product.

Hezbollah secretary-general Naim Qassem rejects the framework agreement signed by Israel and Lebanon, which requires Hezbollah to disarm before an Israeli military withdrawal, and accuses the Lebanese government of legitimizing the Israeli occupation.
Five people are confirmed to have died in rain-related incidents in Afghanistan, over the past 48 hours.
The Israeli military confirms that Walid Haniyeh, a Nukhba Force deputy commander and nephew of former Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh, has been killed in an airstrike in the Gaza Strip.

A Ukrainian Air Force MiG-29 is destroyed by a Russian Geran kamikaze drone on the ground at an airbase in southern Ukraine, while another MiG-29 is lost during a combat mission over Poltava Oblast, with the pilot successfully ejecting and reaching safety.
U.S Secretary of State Rubio says the United States will reengage with GAVI amidst the Ebola outbreak.
Over 10,000 people gather at the Budapest Pride in Hungary, the first pride march in the city since former prime minister Viktor Orbán was voted out in April.
The event occurs following attempts by the Orban government to ban the event and amidst a heat wave in Europe.

CENTCOM conducts retaliatory strikes against Iranian military surveillance infrastructure, communication systems, air defense sites, drone storage facilities, and minelayer capabilities in response to an attack on the Panama-flagged oil tanker M/T Kiku near the Strait of Hormuz, which carried more than two-million barrels of crude oil.
The South Korean ocean ministry reports that two vessels operated by Korean shipping companies have successfully transited through the Strait of Hormuz after being stranded for months during the war.
The confirmed toll of the June 24 earthquakes in Venezuela rises to over 1400 people killed.
Israel says its military has killed Mansour Sami Mahmoud Shahtout, a Hamas naval police commander who ran the Central Camps and took part in the October 7 attacks, in an airstrike in the Gaza Strip.
Central Command says that a fighter jet has fired a Hellfire missile to disable the Botswana-flagged oil tanker M/T Lexie as it was transiting towards Kharg Island.
Iran cancels its participation in technical talks scheduled for today due to recent strikes against the country and unfulfilled conditions of ⁠the memorandum of understanding ceasefire agreement.
The Bahraini Army says on X that Bahrain has successfully intercepted and destroyed "a number" of Iranian missiles and drone attacks on the country.
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi arrives in Baghdad, Iraq, for talks with Iraqi authorities on arrangements for the funeral of former supreme leader Ali Khamenei.

Ukrainian forces launch FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles at strategic targets in Russia, striking the Titan-Barrikady complex in Volgograd, which produces launchers for Russia's Yars and Iskander missile systems.
A separate missile strike destroys a Pantsir missile system in occupied Crimea.
Israel's government unanimously approves recognition of the World War I-era mass killings of Armenians by the Ottoman empire as genocide, pending parliamentary ratification.
Indian petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri says that 12 LPG vessels from India have successfully transited through the Strait of Hormuz without paying tolls.
Afghan foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi summons the chargé d'affaires at the Pakistani embassy in Kabul over the airstrikes.
A court in Kenya blocks the U.S. from opening a new Ebola quarantine facility in the country for three weeks amidst protests that broke out against the facility in which two people were killed.
The death toll from the heatwaves across Europe increases to over 1,300 people killed, including 1,000 in France and over 300 in Spain.

Human rights organizations led by the Raoul Wallenberg Centre for Human Rights reportedly file a complaint with the International Criminal Court against officials from Libya and the United Arab Emirates for their role in atrocities committed in the civil war, most notably the Darfur region.
The National News Agency reports that over 40,000 displaced people have returned to Lebanon since the ceasefire.
Ukrainian oligarch Vadym Iermolaiev is critically injured alongside his wife and daughter after the explosion of a parcel bomb at a building in Monaco, in what seems like an assassination attempt.
Over 150 demonstrators gather at the presidential palace in Cyprus over a Board of Peace multi-day meeting in the country.
Israeli forces hit a tent in central Gaza, killing three Palestinians, including an 8-year old boy.

The Israeli military and Shin Bet in a joint statement says that Israel has killed Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander Talal Jaber Mohammad Abd al-Aal, who was involved in taking hostages during the October 7 attacks including Rom Braslavski.
The U.S. treasury department announces sanctions on two men and nine companies accused of being involved in transportation, financial services, and real estate for the Jalisco New Generation Cartel.
Former Indonesian education minister Nadiem Makarim, who co-founded the super app Gojek, is sentenced to 10 years in prison for corruption.
The South Korean National Assembly approves the nomination of Han Seong-sook as the country's new prime minister, succeeding Kim Min-seok as the country's first female prime minister in 20 years.

The Supreme Court of the United States rules 6–3 that president Donald Trump's executive order restricting birthright citizenship violates the 14th Amendment, with chief justice John Roberts writing that citizenship "was the right to have rights." (AP) (Reuters)

More than 14,000 people participate in rallies organized by the Iglesia ni Cristo (INC) in Metro Manila, Philippines, mainly to support senator and INC member Rodante Marcoleta who is under investigation for plunder.
Five people are arrested at the People Power Monument in Quezon City and three police officers are injured.
Paraguayan president Santiago Peña declares a national holiday after Paraguay defeated Germany 4–3 on penalties, following a 1–1 draw, in the FIFA World Cup round of 32.
The Israel Hayom newspaper reports that the Board of Peace will begin managing humanitarian shelter centers in areas of the Gaza Strip not under Hamas control.
The Sudanese health ministry reports that the total number of cases of cholera in the West and North Kordofan states in the Kordofan region reaches 911, alongside 127 deaths.

According to witnesses, one person is killed and two others are injured when Kenyan police open fire during a protest in Mathare, Nairobi against reported abductions, amid concerns over security abuses.
A truck veers off a road in River Nile State, Sudan, and collides with a passenger vehicle, killing 18 people and wounding another.
At least 24 people are killed in floods and landslides caused by torrential rain in Accra, Ghana, and Abidjan, Ivory Coast.

A coalition of human rights lawyers file a lawsuit against Ghana at the ECOWAS Court of Justice, accusing the country of violating non-refoulement by accepting deportees from the U.S. and forcing them back to the home countries they had fled.
The U.S. state of Arizona reports its first death of the Sin Nombre strain of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome.

Following a fourth round of peace talks, the governments of Israel and Lebanon reach an agreement to renew the ceasefire if Hezbollah ceases its attacks and both countries will implement pilot zones in security zones across Lebanon where Hezbollah militants would be banned.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Ukrainian drones have struck an oil terminal in Saint Petersburg, Russia, amidst the economic forum scheduled to be held in the city and military facilities at a naval base in Kronstadt.
The Kuwaiti defense ministry says that the military shot down 13 ballistic missiles and 17 drones from Iran, during attacks that killed one person and injured 63 at Kuwait International Airport.

Heavy fights erupt with several casualties reported across major routes in Mogadishu after opposition Somali Future Council was attacked by forces loyal to disputed president Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, ahead of planned anti-government protests.
At least 23 people are killed and 40 others are injured in a fire at a building in New Delhi, India.
Agricultural minister John Steenhuisen announces that South Africa has approved vaccines for bird flu.
House of Representatives votes 215–208 to pass a resolution to limit war powers and halt military operations in Iran following previous failed attempts.
A cattle raid in the South Sudanese state of Unity State kills 14 people, including four children.
Local authorities report that more than 60 people are missing after a boat sank on the Aruwimi River the previous day in the Banalia Territory, Tshopo Province, DRC.
The United States House of Representatives passes legislation to provide a new batch of aid to Ukraine and impose new sanctions on ​Russia.
French president Emmanuel Macron says that France and the U.S. plan to establish a ceasefire coordination mechanism, and calls on Hezbollah to give up its weapons to the Lebanese military.

The Israeli military says that the Israeli Air Force and Israeli Navy have conducted strikes in the Gaza Strip killing four Hamas officials and nine Palestinian civilians, in violation of the current ceasefire.

The office of Arizona attorney general Kris Mayes says that it will seek new indictments against fake electors involved in attempting to overturn the 2020 U.S. presidential election in the state following a denial of an appeal by Mayes that would require prosecutors to send the case back to the grand jury.

Authorities in Niger confirm that at least 49 people died of dehydration in an isolated part of the Sahara desert near the country's borders with Algeria and Mali, after their truck broke down while returning from Mali and stranded for several days.

A court in Bogotá, Colombia, orders presidential candidate Abelardo de la Espriella to stop using Colombia's national football jersey as a campaign symbol following a legal challenge filed during the country's presidential runoff campaign.
Around 350 people have been killed in South Darfur during clashes between the Beni Halba and Salamat tribes over the past five days.
Four industrial workers were killed and 11 others were injured of various degrees when an explosion ripped through a shipyard along the Canal del Dique in Pasacaballos, Cartagena, Colombia.

Axios reports that U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have traveled to the Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Tennessee, to talk with nuclear experts who might take part in future negotiations with Iran regarding their nuclear program.

Lebanese president Joseph Aoun and prime minister Nawaf Salam criticize Iran for the rejection of the ceasefire deal with Israel, stating that Lebanon should not be used as a bargaining chip in negotiations between the United States and Iran.
Hotel operator Archipelago International ends management agreements for six hotels in Cuba, citing compliance with United States sanctions.

Scientists at the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom and DIOSynVax reports the first human clinical trial of a AI-designed vaccine for coronaviruses including SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 and potentially Ebola.

Lebanese parliament speaker Nabih Berri rejects the ceasefire deal with Israel, saying it is not a complete ceasefire and does not require an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon at the same time as Hezbollah.

Israeli foreign minister Gideon Sa'ar says that Israel will open its first embassy in Ljubljana, Slovenia, after its new prime minister Janez Janša ordered the Palestine flag at the main government building to be removed within an hour after taking office.

Russian president Vladimir Putin rejects Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy's proposal for a face-to-face meeting, stating that he sees "no point" and "the only point is for the Ukrainian side to halt the advance of our armed forces".
A Malian court sentences a French embassy official to 20 years' imprisonment for undermining state security, and imposes a F.CFA 3.5 million (US$6,225) fine and entry ban.
The United States Department of State approves the potential sale of five Sikorsky SH-60 Seahawk helicopters and related equipment to New Zealand's military in a deal valued at US$1.5 billion.
A Dutch court sentences three men to 47 months' imprisonment for stealing Dacian golden artifacts, including the Helmet of Coțofenești, from the Drents Museum in Assen, Drenthe, in 2025.
The American physician who contracted Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is discharged from the Charité hospital in Berlin, Germany.
The Directorate General of Health Services reports that three children have died from measles in Bangladesh in the past 24 hours.

At least ten people, including three Lebanese soldiers, one of whom is a brigadier general, are killed by Israeli airstrikes on approximately 150 Hezbollah-linked sites across southern Lebanon over two days, including weapon storage areas, command centers, rocket launchers, and other military infrastructure.

Protests following the ballot paper shortages that disrupted some of the Voters' voting during the 2026 South Korean local elections spread to different parts of the country including Daejeon, Busan, and Gwangju.

Several members from Iran, Iraq, and Somalia, along with international sports delegations including referee Omar Abdulkadir Artan, are denied visas and blocked from entering the United States for the FIFA World Cup.
The Bahraini army intercepts three Iranian missiles and several drones launched against Bahrain.
The Kuwaiti defense ministry says that the military intercepted seven Iranian ballistic missiles fired at the country.
The Israeli military announces that it is investigating the incident that killed three Lebanese troops.
A drone strike hits a market in the Abu Zaeima area of Hamrat Al Sheikh in North Kordofan, Sudan, killing 11 people.
U.S. president Donald Trump urges Iran to return to ceasefire negotiations and finalize a deal.
U.S. president Trump threatens that the United States will seize and destroy Iran's highly enriched uranium, with or without their cooperation.

Iranian state media reports that Pakistani interior minister Mohsin Naqvi handed Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi a "written message" from prime minister Shehbaz Sharif for supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei.
At least two people are killed and 11 are injured by Israeli airstrikes in Beirut, Lebanon, which Israel claimed targeted Hezbollah infrastructure, violating the ongoing ceasefire.

The Broadway play Death of a Salesman wins the most Tony Awards in 2026 with six, including Best Revival of a Play, while Liberation, Ragtime, and Schmigadoon! all win the second-most awards with four each, including Best Play, Best Revival of a Musical, and Best Musical, respectively.

Greek police reports that the Anti-Terrorist Service and National Intelligence Service have arrested a Palestinian-born alleged Hamas operative who resides in Crete after he allegedly joined the militant group.
At least 13 Palestinians are killed by Israeli airstrikes across Gaza City, Deir al-Balah, and al-Mawasi, in Gaza, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire.
Former Supreme Court justice and United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Louise Arbour is sworn in as the 31st Governor General of Canada.

Israel publishes a map of southern Lebanon that it will continue to illegaly occupy, and says it may launch attacks beyond it, as Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu rules out a withdrawal of Israeli troops from Lebanon.

Iran announces a pause on peace talks with the United States, and, alongside the Axis of Resistance, announces plans to "completely block" the Strait of Hormuz and threatens to close the Strait of Mandeb, ruling out any further talks until Israel ends its military operations in Lebanon and Gaza.
Moderna announces that it will partner with the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations to develop a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus.
NASA announces that its astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, and Andre Douglas, and ESA astronaut Luca Parmitano will crew the Artemis III mission in late 2027.
The mission's goal is to evaluate rendezvous and docking operations with SpaceX's Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon spacecraft.
Kuwait's army general staff says that its army air defense systems intercepted "hostile" aerial targets.
China imposes sanctions on Philippine defense secretary Gilbert Teodoro, citing remarks he made at the recent Shangri-La Dialogue that China said undermined its interests and bilateral relations.
China also bans him, his wife, and their son from entering the mainland, Hong Kong, and Macau.

John Healey resigns as the United Kingdom's Secretary of State for Defence in protest at a lack of government funding for the British Armed Forces, saying prime minister Keir Starmer is "putting the country’s security at risk" at a time of "growing international threats".
Al Carns, Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for the Armed Forces, also resigns.
Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif says that a ceasefire deal between Iran and the United States has a "final, agreed upon text" to end the war.

Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif and United States president Donald Trump announce that Iran and the U.S. have reached an agreement to end the war, extend the ceasefire by 60 more days, and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with the deal set to be officially signed in Switzerland on Friday.
Indian Petronet liquefied natural gas tanker Disha crosses the Strait of Hormuz, the only known ship to pass since the announcement of the peace deal.
Hungary's parliament approves a constitutional amendment limiting prime ministers' terms to a maximum of eight years in office.
Legislators also remove a constitutional provision linked to the planned dissolution of the Sovereignty Protection Office established under Viktor Orbán.

Brazil's Supreme Federal Court sentences former São Paulo congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro to four years and two months in prison and bars him from holding public office for eight years after convicting him of threatening public officials in connection with U.S. sanctions efforts.

The Recording Academy of the United States announces five new Grammy Award categories for 2027, including Best Asian Pop Music Performance, and revises eligibility rules for Best New Artist, increasing the maximum number of prior submissions from three to four.

Hezbollah states that it received assurances from Iran that the withdrawal of Israeli troops from occupied southern Lebanon will be a demand in the next phase of negotiations with the United States, before any deal about Iran's nuclear program.
Taiwan says the Kenyan foreign ministry revoked visas issued to Taiwanese scientists and prevented them from attending the Our Ocean Conference in Mombasa.
China states that Kenya's actions are consistent with its adherence to the One China policy.
Afghanistan's Taliban government imposes a ban on smartphone use by government employees, with exemptions requiring approval from supreme leader Hibatullah Akhundzada.
Pakistani prime minister Shehbaz Sharif postpones his visit to Switzerland after the memorandum of understanding (MOU) between Iran and the United States was signed remotely.
Ukraine launches its largest ever drone attack on Moscow, Russia, targeting the Moscow Refinery and damaging several residential buildings.
Bolivian president Rodrigo Paz and the Bolivian Workers' Confederation trade union reach an agreement aimed at easing a 50-day protest crisis marked by road blockades and supply shortages.
Malaysian researchers identify Pleurocordyceps cornusynnemata, a new fungal species in Borneo that parasitizes Ophiocordyceps fungi infecting ants.
Cambodia initiates a compulsory conciliation process under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea to address its maritime boundary dispute with Thailand in the Gulf of Thailand.
Turkey exports a warship to Romania, a NATO and European Union member country, for the first time in its history.
Israel accuses Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire negotiated yesterday by launching drones and missiles.
Bolivian president Rodrigo Paz declares a state of emergency, deploying the military to clear the road blockades.

Politico reports that Hungary will abandon its opposition to Ukraine joining the European Union ahead of the upcoming EU conference in Luxembourg after previously blocking it from doing so under former prime minister Viktor Orbán.
Ethiopia's National Election Board reports that prime minister Abiy Ahmed's Prosperity Party will secure a parliamentary majority in the country's general election.
Australia and Canada sign a A$2.5 billion (US$1.7 billion) agreement for the export of Australia's over-the-horizon radar system, the largest defence export deal in Australian history.
The system is intended to support long-range surveillance and monitoring in Northern Canada.
Nepalese police arrest former deputy prime minister and finance minister Bishnu Prasad Paudel on money laundering charges.
The arrest forms part of an anti-corruption campaign launched by prime minister Balen Shah's government following the collapse of the previous administration.
China imposes export controls on 10 U.S. companies and bars government procurement from 46 others in response to a U.S. blacklist targeting Chinese firms.
Keir Starmer announces his resignation as British prime minister and leader of the Labour Party in an address to the nation outside 10 Downing Street, London.
Romania's parliament rejects the proposed government of prime minister-designate Adrian Veștea, which fails to secure the votes required for approval.
President Nicușor Dan is expected to begin a new effort to form a government following the collapse of the nomination.
South Korea announces that it will accept any North Korean prisoners of war captured by Ukraine while fighting for Russia if they choose resettlement in South Korea.
South Korea also opposes any repatriation of such prisoners against their wishes.
Historic Pact's candidate Iván Cepeda concedes defeat in the presidential election won by Abelardo de la Espriella.

Bolivian defense minister Marcelo Salinas and education minister Beatriz García resign amid ongoing anti-government protests, becoming the highest-ranking officials to leave President Rodrigo Paz's administration since the protests began.
France confirms its first Ebola case, and the first case identified outside Africa in this outbreak, after a humanitarian worker returns from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Sri Lanka begins enforcing a nationwide ban on the sale and provision of foods and drinks high in sugar, salt, and fat in schools as part of measures to address rising childhood obesity and related health conditions.

Kishore Vaigyanik Protsahan Yojana (Young Scientist Incentive Plan): National fellowship and scholarship programme to encourage students to take up research careers in the areas of basic sciences, engineering and medicine.
National Social Assistance Programme: Financial assistance to pensioners, widows and other target categories.

Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS): Each MP has the choice to suggest to the District Collector for works to the tune of Rs 5 crores per annum to be taken up in their constituency.

National Scheme on Welfare of Fishermen: Financial assistance to fishermen for construction of house, community hall for recreation and common working place and installation of tube-wells for drinking water.
National Social Assistance Scheme: Public assistance to its citizens in the case of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement and in other cases of undeserved want.
Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS): Setting up of new Eklavya Model Residential Schools and improving existing ones.
Voluntary Disclosure of Income Scheme: Opportunity to the income tax/ wealth tax defaulters to disclose their undisclosed income at the prevailing tax rates.
Infrastructure Facilities for Judiciary: This includes residential facilities, digital facilities, Gram Nyayalayas .
National Child Labour Projects (NCLP): Launched in 9 districts in 1987 and has been expanded in 2005 to 250 districts in 21 different states.
The objective of this project is to eliminate child labour in hazardous industries by 2010.
Interlinking of Rivers Project (ILR, NPP, National Perspective Plan): Development of water resources.
Urea subsidy: The first urea subsidy scheme was in 1977 in the form of Retention Price cum Subsidy scheme (RPS).

International Relations

Key Points: • India was among the very first countries to establish diplomatic relations with Namibia — on 21 March 1990, the very day Namibia formally attained independence from South Africa. • India had long championed Namibian freedom, hosting the SWAPO (South West Africa People's Organisation) representative office in New Delhi and supporting independence through the United Nations.
Background & Additional Information: India was a vocal supporter of decolonization and of the anti-apartheid struggle.
Namibian independence followed UN-supervised elections in November 1989 under UN Security Council Resolution 435.
Post-1990 Developments: India has assisted Namibia through Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) scholarships, capacity-building programmes and lines of credit.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Estonia on 2 December 1991, shortly after Estonia restored independence from the Soviet Union. • India was among the early countries to extend recognition and open formal ties with the Baltic states.
Background & Additional Information: Estonia declared independence on 20 August 1991 during the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
As the USSR disintegrated, India recognized the Baltic republics in line with its support for peaceful change and the sovereignty of the former Soviet republics.
Developments: India–Estonia relations focus on digital technology, IT, cyber security and e-governance.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Ukraine on 17 January 1992, soon after Ukraine's independence referendum of 1 December 1991. • Ukraine has historically been a major supplier of defence equipment and components to India.
Background & Additional Information: Ukraine declared independence on 24 August 1991 and confirmed it in a referendum on 1 December 1991.
India recognized Ukraine early and inherited strong institutional linkages built up during the Soviet era, including in defence manufacturing and heavy engineering.

Developments: Defence cooperation is the bedrock of the relationship — Indian Army T-90 tanks and BMP infantry vehicles use Ukrainian components, and agreements cover repair and overhaul of An-32 transport aircraft and naval engines.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Slovakia on 1 January 1993 — the day Czechoslovakia peacefully split into the Czech Republic and Slovakia. • Slovakia was recognized by India immediately upon the dissolution of Czechoslovakia.
Background & Additional Information: Czechoslovakia split into two sovereign states on 1 January 1993, ending the federation established after the First World War.
Developments: India–Slovakia cooperation spans heavy engineering, machinery, defence (Slovak howitzers have historically been used by India), pharmaceuticals and trade.
Geopolitical Context: India's ties with both Czech and Slovak republics reflect its recognition of the peaceful dissolution of Czechoslovakia and its continued engagement with Central Europe.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Honduras on 28 September 1994. • Honduras is a Central American nation with which India has maintained growing diplomatic and commercial contact.
Background & Additional Information: India opened relations with Honduras as part of its outreach to Latin America and the Caribbean in the 1990s.
Developments: Bilateral cooperation includes trade (especially textiles and pharma), development assistance and capacity-building through ITEC scholarships.
Geopolitical Context: India's engagement with Central America has grown steadily, driven by trade, development cooperation and shared positions in multilateral bodies such as the United Nations.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Palau on 10 April 1995. • Palau became fully independent on 1 October 1994 under a Compact of Free Association with the United States.
India extended recognition and opened formal relations as part of its outreach to the Pacific Small Island Developing States (PSIDS).

Developments: India has supported Palau through the Forum for India–Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC), development assistance, and ITEC capacity-building programmes, including cooperation on climate change and renewable energy.
India's engagement reflects its 'Act East' and SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) policies and its leadership on climate action.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Haiti on 27 September 1996. • Haiti is the first independent nation in Latin America and the Caribbean.
Background & Additional Information: India's engagement with Haiti expanded significantly after the 2010 earthquake, when India provided relief assistance.
Formal relations were established in 1996 as part of India's Caribbean outreach.

Developments: India has contributed police and military personnel to UN peacekeeping missions in Haiti (MINUSTAH/MINUJUSTH), provided lines of credit and development assistance, and cooperated through ITEC capacity-building programmes.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with the Cook Islands in May 1998. • The Cook Islands are a self-governing state in free association with New Zealand.
Background & Additional Information: The Cook Islands, in the South Pacific, have their own government while sharing head-of-state and citizenship arrangements with New Zealand.
Developments: India cooperates with the Cook Islands through the Forum for India–Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC), development assistance and capacity-building, including on climate adaptation.
Geopolitical Context: India's growing engagement with the Pacific Islands serves its objectives of maritime security, multilateral cooperation and leadership on climate change.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with the Dominican Republic on 4 May 1999. • The Dominican Republic is one of the largest economies in the Caribbean.
Background & Additional Information: India opened formal relations with the Dominican Republic in 1999 and later established a resident embassy in Santo Domingo.
Developments: Cooperation includes trade (rice, pharmaceuticals, textiles), investment, tourism and development assistance.
India has extended lines of credit and ITEC scholarships, and both countries cooperate in UN and regional forums.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with the Marshall Islands on 2 February 1997. • The Marshall Islands became fully independent in 1986 under a Compact of Free Association with the United States.
Background & Additional Information: The Marshall Islands is a Pacific island nation, historically significant for India due to its UN voting record on Kashmir.

Developments: Cooperation runs through the Forum for India–Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC), with development assistance, ITEC scholarships and cooperation on climate change, renewable energy and maritime security.

Geopolitical Context: Engagement with the Marshall Islands is part of India's 'Act East' and SAGAR policies, which emphasize maritime cooperation and solidarity with small island states on climate issues.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Timor-Leste (East Timor) on 24 January 2003. • Timor-Leste became fully independent on 20 May 2002, the first new sovereign state of the 21st century.
Background & Additional Information: Timor-Leste regained independence after a UN-supervised transition that followed the 1999 referendum.
India contributed medical and engineering units to the UN peacekeeping mission (UNTAET) and supported the country's reconstruction.
Developments: Cooperation includes development assistance, education, capacity-building and support for Timor-Leste's engagement with ASEAN.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Montenegro on 2 August 2006. • Montenegro became independent on 3 June 2006, after a referendum ended the union with Serbia.
Background & Additional Information: Montenegro's independence dissolved the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro, completing the breakup of the former Yugoslavia.
Geopolitical Context: India's relations with Montenegro are part of its engagement with the post-Yugoslav states and the wider Balkan region.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Monaco on 21 September 2007. • Monaco is a sovereign microstate on the French Riviera, known for finance and tourism.
Background & Additional Information: Monaco is one of the world's smallest states, governed as a constitutional principality.
Geopolitical Context: Relations with European microstates form part of India's broader ties with Europe, focused on investment, finance and multilateral cooperation.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with San Marino on 26 September 2011. • San Marino is one of the world's oldest and smallest republics.
Background & Additional Information: San Marino, an enclave within Italy, claims a founding date of 301 CE.
Geopolitical Context: Engagement with microstates such as San Marino complements India's relations with the European Union and multilateral cooperation.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with South Sudan on 13 March 2012. • South Sudan became the world's newest country on 9 July 2011, gaining independence from Sudan.
Background & Additional Information: South Sudan's independence followed a 2011 referendum mandated by the 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement.
India recognized the new state and opened formal relations, building on a long association with Sudan.
Developments: India has contributed to UN peacekeeping in South Sudan (UNMISS) and provided development assistance, capacity-building and support to the Indian community working there.
Antigua and Barbuda–India relations documents India’s bilateral relations with Antigua and Barbuda.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Armenia on 31 August 1992, after Armenia's independence from the Soviet Union. • India and Armenia have deep historical and cultural ties, including an old Armenian community in India.
Background & Additional Information: Armenia became independent in September 1991 as the USSR dissolved.
India recognized the republic and opened formal relations as part of its outreach to the South Caucasus.
Developments: Cooperation includes defence (India has supplied military hardware to Armenia), pharmaceuticals, IT and education.
Australia–India Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement documents India’s bilateral relations with Australia–India Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Azerbaijan on 28 February 1992, soon after Azerbaijan's independence (declared 30 August 1991). • Azerbaijan, located on the Caspian Sea, is a key energy-producing state in the South Caucasus.
Background & Additional Information: Azerbaijan emerged as an independent republic after the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
India recognized the new state and opened formal relations as part of its outreach to the Caucasus and Central Asia.

Developments: Cooperation includes energy, information technology, transport and connectivity — notably the International North–South Transport Corridor (INSTC), which passes through Azerbaijan linking India with Russia and Europe.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Belarus on 17 April 1992, following Belarus's independence from the Soviet Union. • Belarus is an important partner for India in defence manufacturing and fertilizers.
Background & Additional Information: Belarus declared sovereignty in 1990 and full independence in 1991 as the USSR dissolved.

Developments: Cooperation centres on defence (components and spares used in Indian equipment), potash fertilizers (Belarus is a major supplier to India), heavy earth-moving machinery (BELAZ) and pharmaceuticals.
The two countries have an Inter-Governmental Commission and have explored cooperation in space and civil aviation.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Bosnia and Herzegovina on 10 August 1992, following its independence from Yugoslavia. • Bosnia and Herzegovina declared independence in March 1992 after a referendum.
Background & Additional Information: Bosnia and Herzegovina emerged from the breakup of Yugoslavia amid the Bosnian War (1992–1995).
India extended recognition and contributed to UN peacekeeping efforts in the region.
India has provided humanitarian and development assistance over the years and supports Bosnia and Herzegovina's peace and reconstruction process.
Central African Republic–India relations documents India’s bilateral relations with Central African Republic.
Comprehensive Migration and Mobility Partnership documents India’s bilateral relations with Comprehensive Migration and Mobility Partnership.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Croatia on 9 July 1992, after Croatia's independence from Yugoslavia. • Croatia declared independence on 25 June 1991 and was recognized internationally in January 1992.
India recognized the new republic and opened formal relations as part of its outreach to the successor states.
India and Croatia have signed agreements on economic cooperation and air services, and both work within multilateral bodies such as the United Nations.
India supported the peaceful settlement of the conflicts that accompanied the breakup and established ties with the resulting republics.
Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement documents India’s bilateral relations with Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with El Salvador on 12 February 1979. • The Embassy of India in Guatemala is jointly accredited to El Salvador, while El Salvador maintains an embassy in New Delhi and an honorary consulate in Bangalore.
Background & Additional Information: The Embassy of El Salvador in London was concurrently accredited to India until June 2008, when El Salvador opened its embassy in New Delhi.
The Embassy of India in Panama City was initially concurrently accredited to El Salvador and was later transferred to Guatemala City.

Progress: India and El Salvador signed a memorandum of understanding on holding regular consultations between their foreign ministries in February 2004, and held their first Foreign Office Consultations in August 2012.

Key Points: • Relations between India and Equatorial Guinea existed even before the latter's independence in 1968. • The High Commission of India in Lagos, Nigeria was concurrently accredited to Equatorial Guinea from 2005 until 2008, when accreditation was transferred to the Embassy of India in Luanda, Angola.

Background & Additional Information: Bilateral engagement picked up around 2004, when India's Joint Secretary (West Africa) visited Malabo and Equatorial Guinea signed the TEAM 9 development-cooperation agreement with India.

During ambassador accreditation visits in 2008, both sides discussed a Joint Commission and a General Cooperation Agreement, and Equatorial Guinea requested English-language training for its officials.

Highlights: Prime Minister's Special Envoy Sachin Pilot invited President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo — then chair of the African Union — to the second India-Africa Summit, which President Mbasogo co-chaired with PM Manmohan Singh in Addis Ababa.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Eritrea on 17 September 1993, after Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia on 24 May 1993. • Eritrea's independence followed a long armed struggle and a UN-supervised referendum.
Background & Additional Information: Eritrea formally separated from Ethiopia after a referendum held in April 1993, ending decades of conflict.
India has contributed personnel to UN peacekeeping missions along the Eritrea–Ethiopia border (UNMEE).
Geopolitical Context: Eritrea's position on the Red Sea coast gives it strategic importance for maritime trade.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Georgia on 28 September 1992, after Georgia's independence from the Soviet Union. • Georgia lies on the strategically important South Caucasus corridor between Europe and Asia.
Background & Additional Information: Georgia declared independence on 9 April 1991 and consolidated it after the Soviet collapse.
Developments: Cooperation includes trade, tourism (wine), education and the development of transport corridors linking India with the Caucasus and Europe.
Geopolitical Context: Georgia's position on the Trans-Caspian and Black Sea corridors makes it relevant to India's connectivity ambitions with Europe and the Caucasus region.
India and the International Monetary Fund documents India’s bilateral relations with India and the International Monetary Fund.
India–Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic relations documents India’s bilateral relations with Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic.

Key Points: • India officially established full diplomatic relations with Israel on 21 January 1992. • This decision marked a significant shift in India's foreign policy, which had earlier been more aligned with the Non-Aligned Movement and support for the Palestinian cause.
Establishment of Diplomatic Relations: The establishment of relations came after the end of the Cold War and the start of India's economic liberalization policies.
India's move was influenced by the changing global political landscape and the need to strengthen strategic and economic ties.
Additional Information (Before 1992): Before formal relations were established, India had recognized Israel in 1950 but maintained a cautious approach toward direct diplomatic ties.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Kazakhstan on 22 February 1992, after Kazakhstan declared independence on 16 December 1991. • Kazakhstan was among the first Central Asian republics with which India opened formal ties after the Soviet collapse.
Background & Additional Information: With the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the Central Asian republics emerged as independent states.
India extended early recognition and sought to rebuild historical civilizational, cultural and trade links with the region.
Kazakhstan supplies uranium to India's civilian nuclear programme, and both countries cooperate within the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Kyrgyzstan on 18 March 1992, following Kyrgyzstan's independence from the Soviet Union. • India and Kyrgyzstan enjoy a strategic partnership with close defence and security cooperation.
Background & Additional Information: Kyrgyzstan became independent as the USSR disintegrated in 1991.
India extended early recognition and opened formal ties as part of its outreach to Central Asia.
Developments: Defence and security cooperation is significant, including joint military exercises and training exchanges.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Latvia on 20 December 1991, soon after Latvia restored its independence. • India was among the early countries to recognize the Baltic republics after the Soviet Union dissolved.
Background & Additional Information: Latvia restored independence on 21 August 1991 amid the failed August coup in Moscow and the disintegration of the USSR.
India recognized the Baltic states as sovereign nations and quickly opened formal relations.
Both sides have encouraged investment in logistics and the digital economy, and India's mission in Riga (and the Latvian embassy in New Delhi) facilitate growing commercial links.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Liechtenstein on 6 April 1993. • Liechtenstein is a small, landlocked principality in the Alps, known for finance and manufacturing.
Background & Additional Information: Liechtenstein is one of the world's smallest and wealthiest states, with a constitutional monarchy.
India's relations with the principality grew out of its engagement with European microstates.
Developments: Bilateral engagement is limited but friendly, covering trade, finance and occasional cultural exchanges.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Lithuania on 25 February 1992, following Lithuania's restoration of independence. • Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence (on 11 March 1990).
Background & Additional Information: Lithuania restored full independence in September 1991 as the USSR collapsed.
India recognized the Baltic republics and established formal relations, consistent with its support for the sovereignty of the former Soviet states.
Developments: India–Lithuania cooperation covers lasers and photonics, information technology, education and trade.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Moldova on 20 March 1992, after Moldova's independence from the Soviet Union. • India recognized Moldova soon after it declared independence on 27 August 1991.
India extended recognition and opened formal relations as part of its outreach to the former Soviet republics of Eastern Europe.
Developments: Bilateral cooperation includes trade (India imports wines from Moldova), education, IT and pharmaceuticals.
Interaction is modest but has grown with exchange of delegations and agreements on visa facilitation and cultural cooperation.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Niue on 30 August 2012. • Niue is a self-governing island state in free association with New Zealand.
Background & Additional Information: Niue is one of the world's smallest states, located in the South Pacific.
India opened relations as part of its expanding outreach to Pacific Island countries.

Developments: India cooperates with Niue through the Forum for India–Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC), including development assistance, ITEC scholarships and collaboration on climate change and sustainable development.
Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with North Macedonia (then the Republic of Macedonia) on 9 February 1995. • North Macedonia became independent from Yugoslavia in September 1991.
Background & Additional Information: North Macedonia emerged from the breakup of Yugoslavia.
India recognized the new republic and opened formal relations as part of its outreach to the Balkan states.
North Macedonia and India maintain friendly ties within the United Nations and the Non-Aligned Movement.
India–Papua New Guinea relations documents India’s bilateral relations with Papua New Guinea.
India–Republic of the Congo relations documents India’s bilateral relations with Republic of the Congo.
India–Saint Kitts and Nevis relations documents India’s bilateral relations with Saint Kitts and Nevis.
India–Saint Vincent and the Grenadines relations documents India’s bilateral relations with Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
India–São Tomé and Príncipe relations documents India’s bilateral relations with India–São Tomé and Príncipe.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Slovenia on 18 May 1992, after Slovenia's independence from Yugoslavia. • Slovenia was the first republic to break away from Yugoslavia (25 June 1991).
Background & Additional Information: Slovenia declared independence in June 1991 and was recognized by the international community in early 1992 following the Ten-Day War.
Slovenia supports India's engagement with the European Union, and both countries cooperate in multilateral forums.
Geopolitical Context: The breakup of Yugoslavia in the early 1990s created several new states.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with South Africa on 22 November 1993, ahead of South Africa's first democratic elections in April 1994. • India was a leader of the global anti-apartheid movement, and Mahatma Gandhi developed his philosophy of Satyagraha in South Africa.
Background & Additional Information: India was among the most vocal opponents of apartheid, severing trade and political ties with the apartheid regime.
The establishment of full relations became possible as the system of apartheid was dismantled under President F.W. de Klerk.
A large Indian-origin diaspora in South Africa provided a strong people-to-people link.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Tajikistan on 28 August 1992, after Tajikistan's independence from the Soviet Union. • India operates its first overseas military facility at the Farkhor airbase in Tajikistan.
Background & Additional Information: Tajikistan became independent in 1991 following the Soviet collapse, after which it experienced a civil war.
India recognized the republic and established formal relations as part of its Central Asia outreach.
Developments: India and Tajikistan cooperate closely on defence, security and counter-terrorism, given Afghanistan's proximity.
India–Trinidad and Tobago relations documents India’s bilateral relations with Trinidad and Tobago.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Turkmenistan on 20 April 1992, after Turkmenistan's independence from the Soviet Union. • Turkmenistan is central to India's energy plans through the TAPI gas pipeline.
Background & Additional Information: Turkmenistan became independent in 1991 following the Soviet collapse and adopted a policy of permanent neutrality.
India recognized the republic and opened formal relations as part of its Central Asia outreach.
Developments: The Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India (TAPI) gas pipeline is the flagship project linking Turkmen energy to India.
India–United Arab Emirates relations documents India’s bilateral relations with United Arab Emirates.

Key Points: • India established diplomatic relations with Uzbekistan on 18 March 1992, after Uzbekistan's independence (declared 31 August 1991). • Uzbekistan is the most populous country of Central Asia and a strategic partner of India.
Background & Additional Information: Uzbekistan emerged as an independent republic following the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
India extended early recognition and built on deep historical and cultural ties, including shared Buddhist and Sufi heritage.
